newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London ended mixed after fund buyers again pushed towards resistance at $1,335 per tonne on March. The strong performance in New York despite a rise in US stocks and news of an end to the Colombian dock workers strike, helped encourage London. January closed $9 higher at $1,364 per tonne, while March remained flat at $1,331 per tonne.

In New York the coffee market was able to hold on to gains in spite news of a rapid settlement of the Colombian dock workers strike and yesterday's GCA figures which showed an increase in US green coffee stocks in December. However, later it was reported that Colombian dock workers rejected a preliminary accord and voted to continue their two day old strike at the Pacific coast port of Buenaventura. The strike has caused chaos with Colombian coffee exports, more than 60 per cent of which are shipped through the port. This could aid sentiment on Friday. March added 45 points to close at 123.05 cents/lb while May closed 55 points higher at 119.55 cents/lb. The outer months gained between 0.10 and 1.25 cents/lb.

BRAZIL - Coffee exports in January are expected to reach 1.2 million 60-kg bags. However, given prospects of continued firm domestic prices through autumn traders doubt that the shipping rate can be maintained through to the second quarter of the year. As a result, most believe that without increased government auctions, it is almost impossible for Brazil to ship the 6 million bags it has been allocated between January and June under the ACPC retention scheme.

UGANDA - Coffee exports in October/December 1996 reached 1.291 million 60-kg bags valued at $95.2 million compared to 795,502 bags valued at $88 million the same period the previous year, the Uganda Coffee Development Authority (UCDA) said. In December 1996, a revised total of 514,394 bags valued at $35.85 million were shipped compared to 353,960 bags worth $32.57 million in November. UCDA said the rise in exports over the period was attributable to high levels of closing stocks reported at the end of 1995/96. However, the volumes were also up because the central and eastern coffee districts were at their peak.

INDONESIA - Indonesia's coffee production is expected to be 10 to 15 per cent below the projected 8.0 million 60-kg bags in coffee year 1996/97 (October/September) - the crop year runs from April to March - due to bad weather, the chairman of the Association of Indonesian Coffee Exporters, Oesman Soedargo said. Soedargo also said Indonesia had yet to make a decision on the African initiative to cut coffee exports in the first half of this year. Indonesia so far has been reluctant to back the African proposal because its trade rival Vietnam is not an ACPC member and does not have to cut exports if the plan gets ACPC support.

BRAZIL - Brazil exported 2.192 million bags of coffee in October 1996, sharply up from last year's figure of 1.231 million bags. That brought total exports since the beginning of 1996 (April/March) up to 9.238 million bags, roughly the same what was exported the same period in 1995. Major destinations for green coffee in April/October 1996 were Germany (858,800 vs 546,800 bags), the United States (1.335 vs 1.438 million bags) and Japan (750,600 vs 626,400 bags).

Soluble shipments in April/October 1996 were down to 1.428 million bags from 1.546 million bags the same period last year. Major markets for solubles in April/October 1996 were Russia (461,900 vs 689,300 bags), Ukraine (148,900 vs 3,400 bags), the United States (311,900 vs 220,500 bags) and Japan (139,600 vs 130,400 bags).
